newsitem.title: USA: U.S spot products jump with NYMEX, diffs are mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S spot products jump with NYMEX, diffs are mixed.

text.p: Driven by strength on NYMEX, U.S. spot products prices rose sharply on Tuesday, led by gasolines, industry sources said.

Gasoline grades tacked on about 1.75 cents a gallon from Monday's levels, tracking NYMEX, where concerns about Russian President Yeltsin's health combined with technical strength to inspire buyers. Distillates firmed by 1.50 cents a gallon. The market was also boosted by news of scattered refinery problems, including Coastal's shutting of its 20,000 barrel per day cat cracker in Corpus Christi, Texas last Friday for unspecified unscheduled maintenance.

Traders said the news had not signifcantly moved the market, but reported a slight lift in diffs as a result. Prompt U.S. Gulf conventional gasoline firmed to 3.50 cents under the Nov NYMEX print for early October barrels.
New York harbor gasoline edged higher, but traders noted that the differential gains of about 0.25 cent could be a function of sharp loses on futures market in recent sessions.
Distillates diffs were weaker at both centers, with USG 27th cycle heating oil heard done at 2.60 cents under the September print and prompt low sulfur diesel pegged at 1.75 cents under the screen.
